title: Recipe and Scholarship
premise: Ivo Sandoval, a nonbinary coder at Aldermoor Academy, has kept their identity hidden behind an anonymous forum account for three years — until the school's legendary ghost, the Inkwell, begins leaving notes addressed to them by name in ink that shouldn't exist. Following the notes, Ivo discovers the ghost is the lingering will of the academy's founder, whose dying bargain binds the town's prosperity to a tradition that must be renewed every fifty years, and this year's renewal is failing. As Ivo falls for Wren, the rival scholarship student assigned to help them decode the founder's recipes and cipher-work, they learn that saving the tradition means sacrificing either their anonymity or their future. In the end, Ivo rewrites the founding covenant itself — trading secrecy for truth — binding the town not to one heir's duty but to a found family of students who choose each other.
about_author: Elodie Pemberton is a former boarding-school archivist who spent years cataloguing marginalia in century-old cookbooks before turning to fiction. She writes from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage on the Maine coast, where she insists the ink never dries quite right.

chapters.title: The Account That Knew
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Establishes Ivo's careful double life: brilliant coder by day, anonymous oracle 'mothlight' by night on the school forum. A post predicting a pipe burst comes true, drawing admin suspicion. Emotional beat: the exhaustion of being so careful it hurts, and the first crack in three years of safety.

chapters.title: Ink That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A note appears inside Ivo's locker — addressed to 'Ivo,' a name no one at school uses — written in ink that shifts color and won't smudge. Security cameras show an empty hallway. Emotional beat: wonder colliding with terror; being seen for the first time.

chapters.title: Wren Ashcombe, Assigned
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Headmistress Vane pairs Ivo with Wren, the sharp-tongued scholarship rival, on a 'heritage restoration' project neither wants. Their first clash over the founder's recipe archive reveals Wren reads cipher the way Ivo reads code. Emotional beat: grudging recognition of a mirror.

chapters.title: What the Founder Buried
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In the archive cellar, Wren finds Marguerite Alder's private ledger: recipes interleaved with coded entries about a 'bargain renewed.' The second ghost-note appears, warning: 'Fifty years ends at solstice.' Emotional beat: dread taking root beneath curiosity.

chapters.title: The Tradition That Made the Town
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Research montage through town records: every prosperity boom follows a solstice ceremony; every skipped one brought ruin. Ivo realizes the upcoming centennial renewal coincides with finals week. Emotional beat: the weight of inheritance landing on shoulders that never asked for it.

chapters.title: Notes by Name
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The Inkwell leaves notes for both teens, each eerily personal — quoting Ivo's secret posts, Wren's mother's letters. They compare notes in the library stacks and form a wary alliance. Emotional beat: two lonely people discovering someone else knows what it costs to hide.

chapters.title: First Recipe, First Failure
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Attempting Marguerite's 'Binding Loaf' in the teaching kitchen, the dough turns grey and cold. The oven flame gutters blue. Wren confesses her scholarship depends on pleasing Vane, who wants the project buried. Emotional beat: love against duty, first stirrings.

chapters.title: Vane Knows
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Headmistress Vane corners Ivo, revealing she recognizes mothlight's writing style — and that her own grandmother failed a renewal. She offers protection in exchange for silence about the ledger. Emotional beat: temptation of the safe lie, and refusing it.

chapters.title: The Kitchen at Midnight
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Sneaking into the kitchen after hours, Ivo and Wren succeed where daylight failed — the loaf rises gold, and the ghost manifests briefly as ink swirling in water. A near-touch over the mixing bowl. Emotional beat: intimacy kindled in shared transgression.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Bargain
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Deciphered ledger pages reveal the truth: Marguerite bound her own life-force into the covenant; each renewal demands a willing heir give up their name and future to become the next Inkwell. Emotional beat: horror — the tradition is a beautiful cage.

chapters.title: The Heir Apparent
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The ghost-notes turn urgent and personal: Ivo is the bloodline's last descendant. The covenant names them heir whether they consent or not. Ivo pushes Wren away to protect them. Emotional beat: duty as isolation; choosing loneliness as armor.

chapters.title: Ruin in the Records
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren uncovers that Vane's grandmother didn't fail the renewal — she refused it, and the town's collapse was covered up. Vane has been grooming Ivo as a replacement sacrifice to redeem her family. Emotional beat: righteous fury, and racing to warn Ivo.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Preparations for the centennial ceremony proceed; the whole town unknowingly decorates its own altar. Ivo, resigned, drafts farewell posts as mothlight. Wren breaks through Ivo's walls with the truth about Vane. Emotional beat: love declared against the clock.

chapters.title: The Ceremony Begins
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At the solstice rite, Vane springs her plan — the covenant accepts Ivo's presence as consent. Ink rises like a tide; the ghost's voice fills the hall. Ivo's name begins dissolving from records and memories alike. Emotional beat: erasure as body horror.

chapters.title: What Wren Remembers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Half the town forgets Ivo mid-ceremony, but Wren holds on via the coded letters they've exchanged — love as mnemonic. She storms the ritual circle armed only with Marguerite's ledger. Emotional beat: devotion as defiance.

chapters.title: Rewriting the Covenant
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. In the heart of the ink-tide, Ivo realizes covenants are just code — and code can be forked. With Wren reading out amendments, Ivo patches the founding terms live: consent required, sacrifice optional, community as co-signatory. Emotional beat: climax; authorship as salvation.

chapters.title: The Ghost Chooses
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Freed from obligation, Marguerite's spirit faces a choice: fade, or remain bound. She passes her final note to Ivo — 'You were never careful. You were brave' — and lets go. The ink settles into ordinary black. Emotional beat: grief braided with release.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Miracle
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The town remembers everything; Vane, exposed, resigns but leaves behind her grandmother's true confession, clearing the family name. The covenant now renews through shared stewardship — the kitchen, the archive, the story itself. Emotional beat: exhausted, tender relief.

chapters.title: Signing Our Names
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo deactivates mothlight and posts once more under their real name — a full accounting of the covenant, the ghost, and the truth. Some classmates recoil; most lean in. Emotional beat: the terror and freedom of being legible.

chapters.title: Summer in the Teaching Kitchen
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A sunlit interlude: Ivo and Wren, officially together, teach a summer cohort of volunteer 'stewards' the founder's recipes. First kiss over flour-dusted counters. Emotional beat: joy earned, found family forming around a shared table.

chapters.title: The Next Fifty Years
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. One year later: the stewardship council's first renewal succeeds without sacrifice, witnessed by new notes in ordinary ink — thank-yous, not summons. Ivo mentors a scared first-year who reminds them of their old self. Emotional beat: inheritance transformed into invitation.

chapters.title: Recipe and Scholarship
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, closing frame. Graduation. Ivo and Wren co-author a book — part cookbook, part history, part confession — dedicated 'to whoever is hiding: come to the table.' Final image: a fresh page, waiting. Emotional beat: quiet, complete belonging.
